english: Whom, great one, does death reach? Death reaches cattle. It reaches brothers. It reaches us. And what did not die? Fame did not die. Which fame lives? Good fame lives. Does the ill-famed man vanish? He vanished. Dear one, remember! Good fame stands.
uncertain: méǵh₂: could be VOC 'great one' (addressee) or neuter 'greatly'; read as vocative address
dusḱléwēs: unanalyzed compound dus-+ḱléwes-, read NOM.SG 'ill-famed'
mért/néḱt: aorists read as gnomic or completed events
ḱéywe: VOC of ḱéywos 'dear' (analyzer also offers a PST.1DU of ḱey- 'lie', which does not fit)

english: Lord, how shall I protect my brother? Protect your brother. Do not deceive him. If my brother deceives me, shall I kill him? Do not kill your brother. Ask him and listen to his word. I shall ask my brother. If he asks me for cattle, what shall I give him? Give him half of them. Two brothers are strong. A brother is dear to a brother.
uncertain: h₁íns: masc. ACC.PL 'them', taken to mean the cattle
bʰréh₂terh₁ ... h₁stés: dual; 3DU 'two brothers are' (2DU 'you two brothers are' also possible)
sēmi: adverb 'half', read 'give him half of them'

english: Who, master, is Dyeus? Dyeus is the father of gods and men. What has he seen? He sees us and he sees the gods. Where does he sit? He sits above. Is Earth the wife of Sky? She is his wife and he is her husband. Does he cover the earth? He covers her. Whose daughter is Dawn? Dawn is the daughter of Sky. Dear one (fem.), call upon Dyeus. Dyeus, father, hear us! May Dyeus hear you.
uncertain: dedórḱe: perfect, 'has seen' or present-like 'sees'
dʰéǵʰōm ḱéleti?: NOM or ACC; answer h₁íh₂m̥ ḱéleti shows ACC object, subject = Dyeus
léwbʰeh₂: feminine vocative, addressee is female

english: Who, famous one, steals? He who seized another's cattle, he steals. Does the thief (stealing man) come at night? He comes, and he fears the light. What does he steal? He steals silver and sheep. Who saw him? The dog saw him. What shall the thief give? Whoever steals cattle, let him give them back twice over. Does he who moves the boundary of another's field steal? He does steal. Another's cattle are not one's own.
uncertain: ḱlúte: VOC 'famous one', address
bʰebʰóyh₂e: PRF 1SG or 3SG; 3SG by context
h₂ew: 'back, again'
Hyowdʰéyeti: 'causes to move', i.e. shifts the boundary

english: Great one, I heard an eloquent man. What does he create? He creates fame. Whose fame does he create? He creates the fame of him who slew the serpent. What did he receive? He received a reward. Who gives it to him? The king gives the reward. When the king heard the fame (the song), he rejoiced. What is the reward? The reward is silver and a garment. The reward went away; the fame stands.
uncertain: h₁suwékʷesm̥: unanalyzed compound h₁su-+wékʷes-, ACC.SG 'eloquent one'; could also be read as 'a good speech'
gʷʰént: PST.3SG (imperfect 'was slaying') where a completed event is narrated
h₁ím: masc. ACC 'it' = the reward (misdʰós m.), or 'him' = the poet
léytt: 'went away' (also 'touched'); 'went away' fits

english: The sheep said to the horses: "My heart pains me, seeing a man driving horses."
uncertain: whole line: different unaccented spelling (owis, eḱwobʰyos, eweket, angʰetai, aǵontm̥) not covered by the analyzer; translated from known roots
ǵʰm̥onm̥: 'man (earthling)', not in the lexicon
widontei: DAT.SG participle agreeing with moi 'to me, seeing'

english: How, master, shall we call upon the gods? Call upon them with a true word. Do not call upon them with a lie. To whom do the gods listen? Whoever calls upon them with a true word, him they listen to. Where shall we stand? Stand at the fire and be turned toward them. What shall we say to them? Speak the famous names of the gods. Then ask. They heard it from the heart. They came with their kin and sat down.
uncertain: ǵʰuHéyete: PRS/IMP 2PL; read as imperative
wewr̥tté: perfect imperative 2PL 'be turned toward'
h₁íd ḱr̥dés ḱluwént: AOR 'they (the gods) heard it from the heart'; gnomic or narrative
ḱóymōys: INS.PL; read as adj. 'kin' used as noun ('with their kin'); as noun 'home' it would be 'through the homes', and a goal 'to the homes' would need ACC

english: The Sheep and the Horses
uncertain: title; no verb

english: What did the driver yoke? The driver yoked swift horses to the chariot. What do the horses pull? The horses pull the chariot. And what did the eloquent one (poet) yoke? He yoked words. To what did he yoke them? He yoked them to the mind. The mind is their driver. Who breaks the wheel? The ill-disposed driver breaks the wheel. Dear one, yoke your words and drive them.
uncertain: h₁suwékʷēs: unanalyzed compound, NOM.SG 'eloquent one'
h₁íh₂: neuter ACC.PL 'them' = the words
h₂éǵe: IMP 2SG 'drive'

english: Having heard this, the sheep fled into the field (plain).
uncertain: whole line: unaccented older spelling (owis, aǵrom, ebʰuget) not covered by the analyzer; ebʰuget read as augmented past of bʰewg- 'flee'

english: How shall I learn words? Son, listen and ask. Whom shall I hear? Listen to him who knows. What shall I seek? Seek the true word. Where shall I seek it? Seek it in his home. When I have heard them (the words), what shall I do? Remember them. He who hears well, he learned them. He who works, he learns.
uncertain: h₁ím: alternatively 'him' = the one who knows ('seek him in his home'), which would rescue the masc. form but breaks the what/where question chain
ḱóymoy: LOC.SG 'in the home'
h₁íh₂: neuter ACC.PL 'them' = the words
misfit: h₁ím (twice): masc. ACC.SG, but the antecedent is neuter wékʷos ('seek the true word; where shall I seek it?'); h₁íd expected
h₁uként: AOR 3PL, but its subject só (he) is singular; 3SG h₁éwkt expected (as in the next sentence)

english: Where is the word born? It is born in the heart and it grew in the mind. The mouth does not create the word. The mouth carries it. Where did the word go from the heart? It went to the mouth, and from the mouth it went out to men. What is not born in the heart, that is a lie. How shall my heart become upright? Dear one, listen and learn. A good word is born in a good heart.
uncertain: h₁óh₃s / h₂nérn̥s: ACC of goal with gʷéh₂t
bʰúHeti: SBJV 3SG 'shall become'

english: Master, many streams flow into the sea. Why did the sea not become full? It did not fill. The sun drinks the water of the sea. And where does the water go? It goes up to the sky. Then it rained, and the water went back again. Is the sea deep? It is deep and broad. No one has seen the bottom of the sea. Who arranged this? The gods arranged it.
uncertain: kʷíh₁: INS 'how', used as 'why'
h₂wérst: impersonal AOR 'it rained'
kʷis ... ne: unaccented indefinite + ne = 'no one'

english: What, master, is right? Right is that which the king sets straight. How does he set it straight? A carpenter straightens timber (a tree); the king straightens us. And who makes the king straight? The gods make him straight. Who went astray? He who slipped from the right, he perished. Who is upright? He who speaks the truth, he is upright. Daughter, make your word straight and make your heart straight. The right stands.
uncertain: dóru: 'tree', here timber
h₃réǵeti vs h₃roǵéyeti: 'straightens' vs causative 'makes straight'

english: Lord, how does the poured water reach the gods? Fire carries it to them. And who is Fire? It is the mouth of the gods. The gods eat by means of it. What do we give it? We give it wine and grain. Where does it sit? It sits in the home. In the home it is a guest. Call upon Fire!
uncertain: ǵʰutóm: neuter adj. 'poured' agreeing with wédos (analyzer also offers a 2DU verb form, which does not fit)
h₁íh₁: INS 'with/through it'
h₁ésmey: DAT 'to it/him' = Fire
misfit: h₁stés: 2/3DU 'are (two)', but the subject h₁n̥gʷnís is singular; h₁ésti expected (the answer uses h₁ésti)

english: What, great one, is truth? Truth is that which is. And what is a lie? A lie is that which is not. Who knows the truth? He who saw it, he knows. Who spoke the truth? He who knows, he spoke the truth. How did we come to know the truth? We came to know the truth with the eyes and the mind. Truth stands. The lie fell.
uncertain: méǵh₂: vocative address 'great one'
séngʷt: 'fell, sank'
misfit: dʰrówgʰoh₁: INS.SG or NOM/ACC.DU, but the question needs NOM.SG dʰrówgʰos (as in the answer)

english: What, great one, is a lineage? A lineage is the sons of the fathers. He who was born into a famous lineage bears a famous name. What is a dog's offspring? A dog's offspring is a dog, and a horse's offspring is a horse. Did he become good through his name? He became good through his mind. Where have the fathers gone? They are gone. The name comes from them; fame is one's own.
uncertain: h₁éymos: DAT or ABL PL; read ABL 'from them (the fathers)', DAT 'to them' also possible
ḱléwos swóm h₁ésti: 'fame is (one's) own', asyndetic with the preceding clause
ph₂trṓm: 'of fathers' (also 'of protectors')

english: When it dawned, master, where had the night gone? Dear one, it has gone beneath the earth. And where have the stars gone? They are gone. The light of day overpowered them. Did night come back? It came back. When the sun sank, night came. What does it bring? It brings sleep and cold. Who is awake? The dog and the shepherd are awake. The wolf is coming. Who is afraid? The sheep are afraid. And what are Night and Dawn? They are two sisters. When night goes away, Dawn comes. When Dawn goes away, night comes.
uncertain: h₂wést: impersonal AOR 'it dawned'
wédʰeti: 'leads, brings' (also 'binds, marries'); 'brings' fits
bʰéwdʰetes: 3DU agreeing with dog + shepherd

english: Those who died, where did they go? A deep water lies yonder. Two dogs guard the crossing. How did they go? They went by boat. What do they carry? They carry nothing. Do they come back? From yonder no one comes back. Do they see the sun? They do not see it. Lord, I am afraid. Dear one, do not tremble. The living see the light.
uncertain: h₁yóy ... tóy: relative + resumptive 'those who'
ph₂stés: 3DU agreeing with the two dogs
dedr̥ḱḗr (first): subject = the dead, sóh₂wl̥ ACC object

english: Who, master, are the gods? The gods are heavenly. Where do they dwell? They dwell in the sky. Are they many? They are many. Who is the first of them? Dyeus is the first of the gods. What do they give us? They give us good things. They are the givers of good things. Whom did they come to love? Him who speaks the truth, him they came to love. Are the gods men? They are not. Men die; gods do not die. Son, listen. They have seen us and they heard us.
uncertain: wn̥Hént: AOR 'came to love', possibly gnomic 'love'
m̥rént: gnomic aorist 'die'

english: Who creates a word? He who knows, he creates it. And what does the carpenter build? The carpenter builds a wheel. He builds it from wood. And from what does he (the poet) create it? He creates it from the heart and the mind. How does he arrange them? He arranges them with the mouth. The wheel is swift and the word is swift. A broken wheel does not go. A broken word does not stand. Daughter, arrange your words.
uncertain: dréws: GEN/ABL 'from wood'
h₁ím: masc. ACC 'it' = the wheel (kʷékʷlos m.)
misfit: h₁íh₂ (twice): fem. NOM.SG or neut. NOM/ACC.PL, but the referent is singular neuter wékʷos, elsewhere in the item resumed by h₁íd; neut.PL 'them (words)' is possible but unmotivated; h₁íd expected

english: Who, lord, is Sleep? Sleep is the brother of Death. Does a man die in sleep? He does not die, and he wakes up. He who is gone does not wake. Where does the mind go in sleep? The mind goes yonder and comes back. And where does the mind go in death? In death it goes yonder and does not come back. Daughter, do not fear sleep. When it has dawned, you will wake.
uncertain: mért / bʰéwdʰt / gʷéh₂t: aorists read as gnomic
bʰéwdʰesi: PRS 2SG 'you are awake' or SBJV 2SG 'you will wake'

english: When a man has died, what, famous one, lives on? His name lives and his fame lives. And where is he gone? He is gone. Fire burns him. Does it burn his fame? It does not burn his fame. Is there rest for him? There is rest for him. Who remembers him? His sons remember him. They heard his fame. He went away; fame stands.
uncertain: ḱlúte: VOC 'famous one'
léytt: no expressed subject; read 'he went away'

english: Who, lord, gave a man his name? The father gave the son and the daughter a famous name. When he is gone, who carries it? The sons carry it. Did it vanish? The name of him who deceives vanished. Men heard the fame of him who speaks the truth. Daughter, protect your name. The father's name dwells in the son.
uncertain: dʰéh₁t: 'placed', here 'gave (a name)'
néḱt?: subjectless question, read 'did it (the name) vanish?'
suHnówi: LOC 'in the son'

english: Who, lord, is a good king? The king is the shepherd of men. What does a shepherd do? He protects the sheep from the wolf. When the wolf came to the sheep, the dog and the shepherd drive him away. And who is the king's wolf? His wolf is he who deceives. An ill-disposed king devours his own sheep. The sheep fled from him. What is the wolf's plunder? The wolf's plunder is the lamb and the piglet. When the shepherd protects the sheep, the sheep live.
uncertain: h₂éǵetes: 3DU 'drive' (also SBJV of h₂éǵt 'say', which does not fit)
bʰugént: 'fled' (homonym 'benefited' does not fit)
h₁ludʰét: AOR in a generic when-clause

english: Is the word first, or is thought first? Thought is first. Where does thought lie? It lies in the mind. Then the word comes. Let your mouth not run ahead. The mind (should) drive it. When a word has gone from my mouth, what shall I do? What has gone does not come back. Son, be mindful. Then speak.
uncertain: pró mē drémt: mē + aorist injunctive 3SG, prohibitive 'let it not run forward'
ménos h₁íd h₂éǵe: h₂éǵe is IMP 2SG; ménos must then be VOC ('mind, drive it!') or a second ACC; the sense wants 'the mind drives it'
misfit: h₂éǵe: 2SG imperative where ménos looks like the subject; 3SG h₂éǵeti or h₂éǵetu expected

english: Who, great one, eats grain? He who ploughs the field, he eats grain. And who does not eat grain? He who does not work does not eat. Who received a wage? He who works, he received the wage. Who grew rich in livestock? He who works, he grew rich in livestock. Who pulls the plough? The ox pulls the plough. When he ploughs the field, the earth gives him grain. If he does not plough, the earth gives nothing.
uncertain: h₁áyto: middle aorist 'received'
péḱewh₁: INS 'in livestock' with h₃péwst
kʷid ne: unaccented indefinite + ne = 'nothing'

english: Lord, I heard of the two sons of Sky. What do they (two) do? They drive swift horses. How do they come? They come by chariot. When it dawned, they came. Whom do they protect? They protect men on a ship. When a ship sinks, they come. Where do they dwell? They dwell in the sky. May they protect you!
uncertain: ḱlḗm: analyzed AOR 1SG 'I heard' (homonym 'I leaned' does not fit); the lengthened-grade shape is unusual
gʷm̥tā́m: AOR 3DU 'they came' or IMP 3DU 'let them come'; ACC.SG fem adj. 'passable' does not fit
dʰedʰh₁tés: 3DU 'do'
